Reference: Liu (2026)

Model Setting

The paper studies how legal risk from the permitting process (environmental and land-use permit litigation) affects the entry of utility-scale wind and solar projects in the U.S. Litigation history raises perceived risk and induces regulatory agencies to review permits more cautiously, while legal precedent clarifies legal standards. Because precedent is non-rival and non-excludable, but the developer who pursues an appeal bears the full litigation cost, the model is used to (1) quantify permitting costs in dollars, (2) correct for selection into the observed litigation and appellate sample, and (3) quantify the under-investment in precedent.

Each county-year is a local development market ccc with a finite set of potential projects i∈{1,…,Ic}i\in\{1,\dots,I_c\}i∈{1,…,Ic​}. The game has two stages: in Stage 1, potential developers simultaneously decide whether to enter and start permitting; in Stage 2, entrants that are hit by lower-court litigation decide whether to engage in appellate proceedings (appeal, or defend a favorable ruling against an appeal). Information on market fundamentals is complete; each stage has an idiosyncratic private shock. Developers are short-lived: they anticipate litigation when entering, but take the legal and permitting environment as given and do not internalize how their actions change the environment of future cohorts.

At the start of each period all developers observe the common state:

Sc=(Lc,Dc,Mc,Cc)(8.2.4.1)S_c=(L_c,D_c,M_c,C_c) \tag{8.2.4.1}Sc​=(Lc​,Dc​,Mc​,Cc​)(8.2.4.1)

where LcL_cLc​ is the legal environment (number of past cases, cases with negative outcomes, precedent-setting rulings, lower- and appellate-court caseloads); DcD_cDc​ is the permitting environment (backlog of individual and general permits at the lead agency); McM_cMc​ is electricity market conditions (wholesale prices, PPA prices, demand); CcC_cCc​ is county characteristics (population, median income, Democratic vote share, queued higher-priority projects, zoning ordinances, grid congestion). Each project has observed characteristics xix_ixi​ (fuel type, capacity).

Stage 1: Entry and Permitting

Entering, ei=1e_i=1ei​=1, requires a fixed entry cost CEC_ECE​ (preparing the interconnection request and starting permitting). Every entrant eventually obtains a permit (92% of CWA Section 404 applications are granted), at a one-time permitting cost:

Ciperm=α0+αL′Lc⏟legal cost+αD′Dc⏟institutional cost+αC′Cc(8.2.4.2)C_i^{perm}=\alpha_0+\underbrace{\alpha_L^{\prime}L_c}_{\text{legal cost}}+\underbrace{\alpha_D^{\prime}D_c}_{\text{institutional cost}}+\alpha_C^{\prime}C_c \tag{8.2.4.2}Ciperm​=α0​+legal costαL′​Lc​​​+institutional costαD′​Dc​​​+αC′​Cc​(8.2.4.2)

where αL′Lc\alpha_L^{\prime}L_cαL′​Lc​ captures both the direct effect of litigation risk and the indirect effect through more cautious agency review, and αD′Dc\alpha_D^{\prime}D_cαD′​Dc​ captures agency workload independent of litigation.

Conditional on receiving a permit, the project is litigated in the lower court with probability:

Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1)=Λ(β0+βL′Lc+βx′xi+βC′Cc+εilit)(8.2.4.3)\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)=\Lambda\left(\beta_0+\beta_L^{\prime}L_c+\beta_x^{\prime}x_i+\beta_C^{\prime}C_c+\varepsilon_i^{lit}\right) \tag{8.2.4.3}Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1)=Λ(β0​+βL′​Lc​+βx′​xi​+βC′​Cc​+εilit​)(8.2.4.3)

where Λ(⋅)\Lambda(\cdot)Λ(⋅) is the logistic CDF.

The profit from a completed project is proportional to its computed net present value:

πi=θπ⋅NPVi(Mc,xi,Cc)(8.2.4.4)\pi_i=\theta_\pi\cdot NPV_i(M_c,x_i,C_c) \tag{8.2.4.4}πi​=θπ​⋅NPVi​(Mc​,xi​,Cc​)(8.2.4.4)

and the net profit conditional on completion is:

Πi≡(πi−Ciperm)κcomp(8.2.4.5)\Pi_i\equiv\left(\pi_i-C_i^{perm}\right)\kappa^{comp} \tag{8.2.4.5}Πi​≡(πi​−Ciperm​)κcomp(8.2.4.5)

where κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp is an exogenous completion probability (the project is not withdrawn from the interconnection queue for reasons unrelated to litigation).

The expected payoff from entry is:

Vi(Sc,xi)=(1−Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1))(πi−Ciperm)κcomp+Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1) Wilit(8.2.4.6)V_i(S_c,x_i)=\left(1-\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)\right)\left(\pi_i-C_i^{perm}\right)\kappa^{comp}+\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)\,W_i^{lit} \tag{8.2.4.6}Vi​(Sc​,xi​)=(1−Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1))(πi​−Ciperm​)κcomp+Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1)Wilit​(8.2.4.6)

where WilitW_i^{lit}Wilit​ is the continuation value under litigation (Stage 2). A developer enters if Vi−CE≥εientrV_i-C_E\ge\varepsilon_i^{entr}Vi​−CE​≥εientr​, which gives the logit entry probability:

Pr⁡(ei=1)=exp⁡(Vi(Sc,xi)−CE)1+exp⁡(Vi(Sc,xi)−CE)(8.2.4.7)\Pr(e_i=1)=\frac{\exp\left(V_i(S_c,x_i)-C_E\right)}{1+\exp\left(V_i(S_c,x_i)-C_E\right)} \tag{8.2.4.7}Pr(ei​=1)=1+exp(Vi​(Sc​,xi​)−CE​)exp(Vi​(Sc​,xi​)−CE​)​(8.2.4.7)

Stage 2: Litigation, Appeal and Precedent

A litigated developer chooses ai∈{0,1}a_i\in\{0,1\}ai​∈{0,1}, engaging in appellate proceedings at cost CAC_ACA​. The probability that the project ultimately survives, which nests all lower-court and appellate contingencies, is:

piwin(ai)=Λ(γ0+γL′Lc+γz′zi+γaai)(8.2.4.8)p_i^{win}(a_i)=\Lambda\left(\gamma_0+\gamma_L^{\prime}L_c+\gamma_z^{\prime}z_i+\gamma_a a_i\right) \tag{8.2.4.8}piwin​(ai​)=Λ(γ0​+γL′​Lc​+γz′​zi​+γa​ai​)(8.2.4.8)

The latent payoff from choosing aia_iai​ is:

Uilit(ai)=piwin(ai) Πi−aiCA(8.2.4.9)U_i^{lit}(a_i)=p_i^{win}(a_i)\,\Pi_i-a_iC_A \tag{8.2.4.9}Uilit​(ai​)=piwin​(ai​)Πi​−ai​CA​(8.2.4.9)

The developer appeals if Uilit(1)−εiappeal≥Uilit(0)U_i^{lit}(1)-\varepsilon_i^{appeal}\ge U_i^{lit}(0)Uilit​(1)−εiappeal​≥Uilit​(0), so:

Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)=exp⁡(Uilit(1))exp⁡(Uilit(0))+exp⁡(Uilit(1))(8.2.4.10)\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)=\frac{\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)\right)}{\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(0)\right)+\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)\right)} \tag{8.2.4.10}Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)=exp(Uilit​(0))+exp(Uilit​(1))exp(Uilit​(1))​(8.2.4.10)

Define the private incremental value of appealing:

λi≡(piwin(1)−piwin(0))Πi−CA(8.2.4.11)\lambda_i\equiv\left(p_i^{win}(1)-p_i^{win}(0)\right)\Pi_i-C_A \tag{8.2.4.11}λi​≡(piwin​(1)−piwin​(0))Πi​−CA​(8.2.4.11)

Then the continuation value under litigation is:

Wilit=ζ(piwin(0) Πi+Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1) λi)(8.2.4.12)W_i^{lit}=\zeta\left(p_i^{win}(0)\,\Pi_i+\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)\,\lambda_i\right) \tag{8.2.4.12}Wilit​=ζ(piwin​(0)Πi​+Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)λi​)(8.2.4.12)

where ζ\zetaζ governs the sensitivity of entry to the expected appeal value.

Not every appellate decision creates precedent. Conditional on appeal, a binding precedent is set with probability:

ψi=Λ(ψ0+ψL′Lc+ψz′zi)(8.2.4.13)\psi_i=\Lambda\left(\psi_0+\psi_L^{\prime}L_c+\psi_z^{\prime}z_i\right) \tag{8.2.4.13}ψi​=Λ(ψ0​+ψL′​Lc​+ψz′​zi​)(8.2.4.13)

which depends on institutional legal factors (court level, motions, affirmed/remanded, summary judgment, relief against the authority), not on the developer's actions.

Legal Precedent as an Externality

One precedent shifts future lower-court litigation outcomes by δα>0\delta_\alpha>0δα​>0 and δβ>0\delta_\beta>0δβ​>0. Let pˉlit\bar{p}^{lit}pˉ​lit be the baseline litigation probability of future projects, Πˉfut\bar{\Pi}^{fut}Πˉfut the expected surplus of a completed future project and NfutN^{fut}Nfut the size of the next cohort of potential entrants. The social surplus of one precedent is:

Ω=[δα(1−pˉlit)+δβ pˉlit]κcomp ΠˉfutNfut(8.2.4.14)\Omega=\left[\delta_\alpha\left(1-\bar{p}^{lit}\right)+\delta_\beta\,\bar{p}^{lit}\right]\kappa^{comp}\,\bar{\Pi}^{fut}N^{fut} \tag{8.2.4.14}Ω=[δα​(1−pˉ​lit)+δβ​pˉ​lit]κcompΠˉfutNfut(8.2.4.14)

The external benefit of project iii's appellate engagement is Ωi=λiΩ\Omega_i=\lambda_i\OmegaΩi​=λi​Ω, where the weight λi∈[0,1]\lambda_i\in[0,1]λi​∈[0,1] is the likelihood that iii's appeal creates binding precedent (in the paper this reuses the symbol λi\lambda_iλi​; it plays the role of ψi\psi_iψi​). Developers ignore Ωi\Omega_iΩi​ when choosing aia_iai​, while the social continuation value is:

Wilit,soc=Piappeal(λi+Ωi)(8.2.4.15)W_i^{lit,soc}=P_i^{appeal}\left(\lambda_i+\Omega_i\right) \tag{8.2.4.15}Wilit,soc​=Piappeal​(λi​+Ωi​)(8.2.4.15)

Hence private appeal, and thus precedent formation, is below the social optimum.

Correlated Unobservables

Observed lawsuits and appeals are a selected sample (financial resources, legal sophistication, project quality, risk tolerance). The latent shocks of the three stages are drawn jointly:

(νientryνilitνiappeal)∼N(0,Σ),Σ=(1ρELρEAρEL1ρLAρEAρLA1)(8.2.4.16)\begin{pmatrix}\nu_i^{entry}\\ \nu_i^{lit}\\ \nu_i^{appeal}\end{pmatrix}\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\Sigma),\qquad \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho_{EL}&\rho_{EA}\\ \rho_{EL}&1&\rho_{LA}\\ \rho_{EA}&\rho_{LA}&1\end{pmatrix} \tag{8.2.4.16}​νientry​νilit​νiappeal​​​∼N(0,Σ),Σ=​1ρEL​ρEA​​ρEL​1ρLA​​ρEA​ρLA​1​​(8.2.4.16)

with the normalization ρEA=0\rho_{EA}=0ρEA​=0. The draws are transformed to uniforms uij=Φ(νij)u_i^j=\Phi(\nu_i^j)uij​=Φ(νij​), j∈{entry,lit,appeal}j\in\{entry,lit,appeal\}j∈{entry,lit,appeal}, which are then used in the logit choices, so that the composition of litigated and appealed projects differs from the population of entrants.

Net Profit of Potential Entrants

Capacity and fuel type of potential entrants are bootstrapped from actual entrants in the same county-year (or state-year). Annual generation and revenue are:

Qi=MWi×CFi×(1−Curtaili)×8760,Ri=Qi×(Piwholesale+Pippa)(8.2.4.17)Q_i=MW_i\times CF_i\times(1-Curtail_i)\times 8760,\qquad R_i=Q_i\times\left(P_i^{wholesale}+P_i^{ppa}\right) \tag{8.2.4.17}Qi​=MWi​×CFi​×(1−Curtaili​)×8760,Ri​=Qi​×(Piwholesale​+Pippa​)(8.2.4.17)

where CFiCF_iCFi​ is the state-level technology-specific capacity factor, PwholesaleP^{wholesale}Pwholesale is the peak-hour wholesale price (ReWEP, imputed with EIA-923 resale prices) and PppaP^{ppa}Pppa is the regional PPA price (LBNL). With r=0.05r=0.05r=0.05 and a 25-year lifetime:

NPVi=(Ri−CiO&M)×1−(1+r)−25r,πi=NPVi−Fi(8.2.4.18)NPV_i=\left(R_i-C_i^{O\&M}\right)\times\frac{1-(1+r)^{-25}}{r},\qquad \pi_i=NPV_i-F_i \tag{8.2.4.18}NPVi​=(Ri​−CiO&M​)×r1−(1+r)−25​,πi​=NPVi​−Fi​(8.2.4.18)

where FiF_iFi​ is the technology-specific capital cost (EIA).

Estimation

The parameters are recovered in three steps.

(1) Calibration, Θcalibrate=[ctlit,κcomp]\Theta^{calibrate}=[ct^{lit},\kappa^{comp}]Θcalibrate=[ctlit,κcomp]. State trial-court cases are not fully observed, so the lower-court litigation count ctlitct^{lit}ctlit (state-year) is imputed from state appellate cases using the federal appellate-to-trial ratio (0.25), and distributed over years with the federal lag distribution (weights 0.39, 0.39, 0.16, 0.06 for lags of 0–1, 1–2, 2–3, 3–4 years). The completion shock κ\kappaκ is the exogenous withdrawal rate by transmission owner-year in the interconnection queues (2010–2024).

(2) Probit outside the model, Θprobit=[ψ]\Theta^{probit}=[\psi]Θprobit=[ψ] (10 parameters): precedent formation conditional on appeal, using court-level and case-level legal characteristics. Since precedent formation is determined by courts and not by developers, it can be estimated separately.

(3) SMM for the remaining 23 parameters:

ΘSMM=[CE,α,θπ⏟Entry / Permit, CA,ζ,γ,ψ0⏟Appeal / Precedent, ρEL,ρLA⏟Selection Corr](8.2.4.19)\Theta^{SMM}=[\underbrace{C_E,\alpha,\theta_\pi}_{\text{Entry / Permit}},\ \underbrace{C_A,\zeta,\gamma,\psi_0}_{\text{Appeal / Precedent}},\ \underbrace{\rho_{EL},\rho_{LA}}_{\text{Selection Corr}}] \tag{8.2.4.19}ΘSMM=[Entry / PermitCE​,α,θπ​​​, Appeal / PrecedentCA​,ζ,γ,ψ0​​​, Selection CorrρEL​,ρLA​​​](8.2.4.19)

where α\alphaα has 12 elements and γ\gammaγ has 4.

Simulation: for each county-year, the number of potential entrants is the maximum number of actual entrants ever observed in that county. Continuation values of the appellate stage are computed first by backward induction, then entry is simulated forward with the logit. Among entrants in each state-year, exactly ctlitct^{lit}ctlit projects are assigned to litigation by an exponential race: each entrant gets a random clock that ticks faster when its logistic litigation propensity (driven by z2z_2z2​) is higher, shifted by a common constant so that the total matches ctlitct^{lit}ctlit; the first clocks to go off are litigated. Litigated projects then make appeal decisions, and appeal outcomes and precedent formation are simulated.

The estimator matches K=40K=40K=40 moments (mostly counts by bins):

Θ^=arg⁡min⁡Θ g(Θ)′Wg(Θ),W=Ω^−1(8.2.4.20)\hat{\Theta}=\arg\min_{\Theta}\ g(\Theta)^{\prime}Wg(\Theta),\qquad W=\hat{\Omega}^{-1} \tag{8.2.4.20}Θ^=argΘmin​ g(Θ)′Wg(Θ),W=Ω^−1(8.2.4.20)

where g(Θ)g(\Theta)g(Θ) is the vector of percentage deviations between simulated moments M(Θ)M(\Theta)M(Θ) and empirical moments MMM, and Ω^\hat{\Omega}Ω^ is the variance-covariance matrix of the empirical moments from 200 bootstrap replications. The objective is minimized with a genetic algorithm. Standard errors come from:

S(Θ^−Θ0)→dN(0,(G′WG)−1G′WΩWG(G′WG)−1)(8.2.4.21)\sqrt{S}\left(\hat{\Theta}-\Theta_0\right)\xrightarrow{d}\mathcal{N}\left(0,\left(G^{\prime}WG\right)^{-1}G^{\prime}W\Omega WG\left(G^{\prime}WG\right)^{-1}\right) \tag{8.2.4.21}S​(Θ^−Θ0​)d​N(0,(G′WG)−1G′WΩWG(G′WG)−1)(8.2.4.21)

with the Jacobian GGG computed by finite differences.

Identification

  • CEC_ECE​: overall level of entry.

  • α0,αL,αD,αC\alpha_0,\alpha_L,\alpha_D,\alpha_Cα0​,αL​,αD​,αC​: entry across bins of the legal environment, permit backlog and county characteristics.

  • θπ\theta_\piθπ​: response of entry to computed project NPV.

  • CAC_ACA​: overall appeal frequency among litigated projects, and its variation across lower-court caseload z2z_2z2​, appellate caseload z3z_3z3​ and legal environment bins.

  • γ0,γL\gamma_0,\gamma_Lγ0​,γL​: appeal win rates, overall and across legal environment bins.

  • ψ0\psi_0ψ0​: overall frequency with which appeals create precedent.

The correlations are identified by stage-specific excluded shifters:

  • z1z_1z1​: transmission line density in 1993, which proxies long-run siting fundamentals and grid access and shifts entry only.

  • z2z_2z2​: lower-court caseload (backlog), which shifts litigation through longer expected processing time and is excluded from entry payoffs and appeal decisions.

  • z3z_3z3​: appellate caseload, which shifts appeal conditional on litigation.

ρEL\rho_{EL}ρEL​ is identified from variation in entry across z2z_2z2​ bins conditional on z1z_1z1​: since z2z_2z2​ only shifts litigation, systematic differences in entry across z2z_2z2​ must come from correlated unobservables. ρLA\rho_{LA}ρLA​ is identified from appeal rates among litigated projects across z2z_2z2​ bins, which reflect the composition of the litigated pool. (ρEA\rho_{EA}ρEA​ would be identified from entry across z3z_3z3​ bins, but is normalized to 0.)

Key Estimates

  • Entry cost C^E=0.500\hat{C}_E=0.500C^E​=0.500 ($M), profit sensitivity θ^π=0.077\hat{\theta}_\pi=0.077θ^π​=0.077.

  • Legal cost: overall litigation raises permitting cost (α^L1=0.672\hat{\alpha}_{L1}=0.672α^L1​=0.672), negative-outcome litigation has a small effect (α^L2=0.089\hat{\alpha}_{L2}=0.089α^L2​=0.089), and precedent-setting litigation lowers it (α^L3=−0.258\hat{\alpha}_{L3}=-0.258α^L3​=−0.258).

  • Institutional cost: backlog of individual permits lowers cost (α^D1=−0.138\hat{\alpha}_{D1}=-0.138α^D1​=−0.138, larger and better-capitalized developers), backlog of general permits raises it (α^D2=0.097\hat{\alpha}_{D2}=0.097α^D2​=0.097); local zoning ordinances raise it substantially (α^C6=2.285\hat{\alpha}_{C6}=2.285α^C6​=2.285).

  • Permitting cost among entrants with positive NPV: median $4.4M, mean $5.5M, 90th percentile $8.8M; as a share of net profit: 6% at the median, 14% on average, over 40% in the upper tail.

  • Appeal cost C^A=0.536\hat{C}_A=0.536C^A​=0.536 ($M); sensitivity to appeal value ζ^=0.841\hat{\zeta}=0.841ζ^​=0.841; γ^0=−4.977\hat{\gamma}_0=-4.977γ^​0​=−4.977, ψ^0=0.062\hat{\psi}_0=0.062ψ^​0​=0.062.

  • Selection: raw ρ^EL=0.922\hat{\rho}_{EL}=0.922ρ^​EL​=0.922 and ρ^LA=0.764\hat{\rho}_{LA}=0.764ρ^​LA​=0.764, corresponding to correlations of 0.726 and 0.441.

  • Fit: simulated entry 16,395 vs. 15,570 observed; appeals 253 vs. 250; precedents 157 vs. 157; appeal wins 147 vs. 177 (outcomes of appeals do not depend on case characteristics).

Counterfactuals

Baseline simulated entry is 16,395 projects.

  • Maximal precedent (comparative static): each county is given its maximum observed level of precedent from the start. Entry rises to 16,818 (+2.6%), the informational value of legal clarity alone.

  • Legal fee-shifting: prevailing parties recover attorney and expert fees (as in the Clean Air Act citizen-suit provision), modeled as a 5–40% reduction in CAC_ACA​. A 20% reduction raises entry to 17,388 (+6.1%).

  • Legal protection insurance: the same 20% reduction in CAC_ACA​, but developers pay an upfront premium proxied by 20/K20/K20/K percent of expected net profit (K=15K=15K=15). Entry rises by 1.6%.

  • Streamlined permitting: a 5–40% reduction in CpermC^{perm}Cperm. A 20% reduction raises entry to 16,946 (+3.4%).

Policies that directly lower the private cost of legal proceedings, and thus address the under-investment in precedent, raise entry more than administrative reforms that only lower permitting costs.

The vector ScS_cSc​ is the common-knowledge state of local market ccc (a county-year). It collects everything that all potential developers observe before they move, and it is the conditioning set of every probability and value function in the model. It has four blocks. LcL_cLc​ is the legal environment: the stock of past permit lawsuits, the number of those with negative outcomes, the number that set precedent, and the caseloads of the lower and appellate courts. DcD_cDc​ is the permitting environment: the backlog of individual and general permits at the lead agency. McM_cMc​ is electricity market conditions: wholesale prices, PPA prices, demand. CcC_cCc​ is county characteristics: population, income, Democratic vote share, higher-queued projects, zoning ordinances, grid congestion.

Each block enters through a different channel. LcL_cLc​ shifts the permitting cost in equation (2), the litigation probability in equation (3), the win probability in equation (8) and the precedent probability in equation (13). DcD_cDc​ enters only the permitting cost in equation (2). McM_cMc​ enters only through the net present value in equation (4). CcC_cCc​ enters equations (2), (3) and (4).

Two assumptions are packed into this definition. First, information about ScS_cSc​ is complete, so the only private information is the idiosyncratic shocks of equation (16), and each developer's problem can be solved without modelling beliefs about rivals' states. Second, ScS_cSc​ is taken as given: developers are short-lived and do not internalize that an appeal today changes the legal environment of tomorrow. Formally there is no law of motion

Lcnext=h(Lc,{ai}i)L_{c}^{\text{next}}=h\left(L_c,\{a_i\}_{i}\right)Lcnext​=h(Lc​,{ai​}i​)

inside any developer's problem, even though such a mapping exists in reality. The model is therefore a sequence of static two-stage games, and the missing dynamic link is exactly the externality quantified in equations (14) and (15). For identification, the paper adds a timing assumption: ScS_cSc​ evolves slowly and is independent of the stage-specific shocks.

This is an assumed functional form: the one-time permitting cost is a linear index in the market state. α0\alpha_0α0​ is a baseline cost common to all markets. αL′Lc\alpha_L^{\prime}L_cαL′​Lc​ is the legal cost: it loads on the number of past cases, negative-outcome cases and precedent-setting cases, and it bundles the direct effect of litigation risk with the indirect effect of agencies reviewing more cautiously where they have been sued before. αD′Dc\alpha_D^{\prime}D_cαD′​Dc​ is the institutional cost from agency workload, unrelated to litigation. αC′Cc\alpha_C^{\prime}C_cαC′​Cc​ absorbs county characteristics such as zoning ordinances. In total α\alphaα has 12 elements (a constant, 3 legal, 2 permitting and 6 county loadings). The cost is read in millions of dollars.

Although the left-hand side carries the subscript iii, the right-hand side depends only on ccc: all projects in the same county-year face the same permitting cost, and there is no unobserved cost heterogeneity. Linearity means that each element of α\alphaα is a constant marginal cost. For two markets that differ only by one unit in a single legal variable Lc,kL_{c,k}Lc,k​,

ΔCperm=αLk\Delta C^{perm}=\alpha_{Lk}ΔCperm=αLk​

so the estimate 0.672 for past cases reads as 0.67 million dollars per unit, and the estimate of −0.258-0.258−0.258 for precedent-setting cases as a saving of 0.26 million dollars.

The cost is never observed. It is recovered by revealed preference: it enters the entry payoff through Πi\Pi_iΠi​ in equation (5) and ViV_iVi​ in equation (6), so α\alphaα is identified from how entry counts in equation (7) vary across bins of LcL_cLc​, DcD_cDc​ and CcC_cCc​, holding computed profitability fixed. In the absence of litigation risk the marginal effect on the entry payoff is

∂Vi∂Ciperm=−κcomp\frac{\partial V_i}{\partial C_i^{perm}}=-\kappa^{comp}∂Ciperm​∂Vi​​=−κcomp

Note an implicit assumption: because the cost appears inside (πi−Ciperm)κcomp(\pi_i-C_i^{perm})\kappa^{comp}(πi​−Ciperm​)κcomp, it is paid only in the state where the project is completed (and, in Stage 2, survives litigation). A permitting cost that is sunk before completion would instead enter without the factor κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp.

This is the assumed lower-court litigation risk of a permitted project. The index inside the logistic CDF Λ(x)=ex/(1+ex)\Lambda(x)=e^{x}/(1+e^{x})Λ(x)=ex/(1+ex) depends on the legal environment LcL_cLc​ (a history of lawsuits signals organized opposition and experienced plaintiffs), on project characteristics xix_ixi​ (fuel type and capacity, since larger projects attract more challenges), on county characteristics CcC_cCc​, and on an unobserved litigation shock εilit\varepsilon_i^{lit}εilit​. The logistic form keeps the probability in the unit interval and makes each coefficient a log-odds effect:

log⁡Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1)1−Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1)=β0+βL′Lc+βx′xi+βC′Cc+εilit\log\frac{\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)}{1-\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)}=\beta_0+\beta_L^{\prime}L_c+\beta_x^{\prime}x_i+\beta_C^{\prime}C_c+\varepsilon_i^{lit}log1−Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1)Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1)​=β0​+βL′​Lc​+βx′​xi​+βC′​Cc​+εilit​

A notational caveat: as written, following the paper, the shock sits inside Λ(⋅)\Lambda(\cdot)Λ(⋅), so the object is a probability conditional on εilit\varepsilon_i^{lit}εilit​, that is, a project-specific propensity. The probability a developer uses in equation (6) is this propensity; the econometrician would have to integrate over the shock. Litigation is a risk imposed by third parties, not a choice of the developer.

The equation is schematic in the estimation: the vector β\betaβ is not estimated. The number of litigated projects per state-year, ctlitct^{lit}ctlit, is calibrated, and an exponential race assigns which entrants are sued. In the standard form of that device, entrant iii draws a clock TiT_iTi​ that is exponential with rate wiw_iwi​ equal to its logistic propensity (driven by the lower-court caseload z2z_2z2​ and the correlated draw from equation (16)), and the first ctlitct^{lit}ctlit clocks to ring are litigated. The probability of being selected first is

Pr⁡(Ti=min⁡jTj)=wi∑jwj\Pr\left(T_i=\min_j T_j\right)=\frac{w_i}{\sum_j w_j}Pr(Ti​=jmin​Tj​)=∑j​wj​wi​​

so the count is matched exactly while relative risks still follow the logistic index. This probability then weights the two branches of the entry payoff in equation (6).

Gross profit from a completed project is assumed proportional to a net present value that the researcher computes outside the model from market conditions McM_cMc​ (prices), project characteristics xix_ixi​ (technology, capacity) and county characteristics CcC_cCc​; the construction is in equations (17) and (18). The scalar θπ>0\theta_\pi>0θπ​>0 is estimated. It converts the engineering-style NPV into the payoff that actually drives entry, and it is identified from how entry counts vary across bins of computed NPV. The estimate is 0.077.

Why a scaling parameter is needed: the computed NPV is a noisy and probably inflated proxy (state-level capacity factors, regional prices, no financing costs, taxes or risk premia), and the entry shock in equation (7) has a fixed unit scale. Writing out the deterministic part of the entry index without litigation,

Vi−CE=κcomp(θπNPVi−Ciperm)−CEV_i-C_E=\kappa^{comp}\left(\theta_\pi NPV_i-C_i^{perm}\right)-C_EVi​−CE​=κcomp(θπ​NPVi​−Ciperm​)−CE​

shows that θπ\theta_\piθπ​ is the coefficient on dollars of computed NPV, while the coefficient on CipermC_i^{perm}Ciperm​ is normalized to one. Reading CipermC_i^{perm}Ciperm​, CEC_ECE​ and CAC_ACA​ in millions of dollars therefore relies on the unstated normalization that the logistic shock has scale one in million-dollar units and that θπ\theta_\piθπ​ only deflates a mismeasured NPV. Under the alternative reading, in which computed NPV is true dollar profit and θπ\theta_\piθπ​ is the marginal utility of a dollar, the money-metric costs would be α/θπ\alpha/\theta_\piα/θπ​, about 13 times larger. The two readings are observationally equivalent.

There is also an inconsistency of notation with equation (18). There the appendix defines NPViNPV_iNPVi​ as the discounted operating margin and sets πi=NPVi−Fi\pi_i=NPV_i-F_iπi​=NPVi​−Fi​, without θπ\theta_\piθπ​. The consistent reading is that the argument of equation (4) is the net-of-capital-cost profit of equation (18), so that the payoff used in the model is θπ(NPVi−Fi)\theta_\pi(NPV_i-F_i)θπ​(NPVi​−Fi​).

This identity defines the payoff unit used in the rest of the model. Take gross profit πi\pi_iπi​ from equation (4), subtract the permitting cost CipermC_i^{perm}Ciperm​ from equation (2), and multiply by κcomp∈[0,1]\kappa^{comp}\in[0,1]κcomp∈[0,1], the probability that the project is not withdrawn from the interconnection queue for reasons unrelated to litigation (calibrated as one minus the exogenous withdrawal rate by transmission owner and year). A withdrawn project pays zero, so

Πi=κcomp(πi−Ciperm)+(1−κcomp)⋅0\Pi_i=\kappa^{comp}\left(\pi_i-C_i^{perm}\right)+\left(1-\kappa^{comp}\right)\cdot 0Πi​=κcomp(πi​−Ciperm​)+(1−κcomp)⋅0

The paper calls Πi\Pi_iΠi​ the net profit conditional on successful completion, but because it already contains κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp it is really the expected net profit before the completion shock is realized; the profit conditional on completion is πi−Ciperm\pi_i-C_i^{perm}πi​−Ciperm​.

Πi\Pi_iΠi​ is the prize at every later node. It is the payoff of a non-litigated entrant in equation (6), the amount at stake in litigation in equation (9), and the base of the incremental value of appealing in equation (11) and of the continuation value in equation (12). Three implications follow. First, κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp scales down profits and permitting costs alike, so a higher withdrawal rate dampens the response of entry to both. Second, the completion shock is independent of litigation and of the private shocks. Third, Πi\Pi_iΠi​ can be negative for projects with low NPV in high-cost counties; for them winning in court has negative value, and such projects enter only on a large favorable entry shock. Substituting equation (2) gives the object that the data discipline:

Πi=κcomp(θπNPVi−α0−αL′Lc−αD′Dc−αC′Cc)\Pi_i=\kappa^{comp}\left(\theta_\pi NPV_i-\alpha_0-\alpha_L^{\prime}L_c-\alpha_D^{\prime}D_c-\alpha_C^{\prime}C_c\right)Πi​=κcomp(θπ​NPVi​−α0​−αL′​Lc​−αD′​Dc​−αC′​Cc​)

The entry payoff is an expectation over what happens after the permit is granted. Write PiL≡Pr⁡(Li=1∣ei=1)P_i^{L}\equiv\Pr(L_i=1\mid e_i=1)PiL​≡Pr(Li​=1∣ei​=1) for the litigation probability of equation (3) and PiA≡Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)P_i^{A}\equiv\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)PiA​≡Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1) for the appeal probability of equation (10).

Branch 1, no litigation (probability 1−PiL1-P_i^{L}1−PiL​). The project proceeds to the interconnection queue. With probability κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp it is completed and earns πi−Ciperm\pi_i-C_i^{perm}πi​−Ciperm​; otherwise it earns zero. The expected payoff is

κcomp(πi−Ciperm)+(1−κcomp)⋅0=Πi\kappa^{comp}\left(\pi_i-C_i^{perm}\right)+\left(1-\kappa^{comp}\right)\cdot 0=\Pi_iκcomp(πi​−Ciperm​)+(1−κcomp)⋅0=Πi​

by equation (5).

Branch 2, litigation (probability PiLP_i^{L}PiL​). The developer moves to Stage 2, whose expected value is WilitW_i^{lit}Wilit​, derived in equation (12).

The law of total expectation over the two branches gives the target:

Vi(Sc,xi)=(1−PiL)Πi+PiL Wilit=(1−PiL)(πi−Ciperm)κcomp+PiL Wilit\begin{aligned} V_i(S_c,x_i)&=\left(1-P_i^{L}\right)\Pi_i+P_i^{L}\,W_i^{lit}\\ &=\left(1-P_i^{L}\right)\left(\pi_i-C_i^{perm}\right)\kappa^{comp}+P_i^{L}\,W_i^{lit} \end{aligned}Vi​(Sc​,xi​)​=(1−PiL​)Πi​+PiL​Wilit​=(1−PiL​)(πi​−Ciperm​)κcomp+PiL​Wilit​​

The fixed entry cost CEC_ECE​ is not part of ViV_iVi​; it is subtracted in the entry rule of equation (7).

To see what litigation does to the incentive to enter, substitute equation (12):

Vi=(1−PiL)Πi+PiLζ(piwin(0) Πi+PiAλi)=Πi−PiL[(1−ζ piwin(0))Πi−ζ PiAλi]\begin{aligned} V_i&=\left(1-P_i^{L}\right)\Pi_i+P_i^{L}\zeta\left(p_i^{win}(0)\,\Pi_i+P_i^{A}\lambda_i\right)\\ &=\Pi_i-P_i^{L}\left[\left(1-\zeta\,p_i^{win}(0)\right)\Pi_i-\zeta\,P_i^{A}\lambda_i\right] \end{aligned}Vi​​=(1−PiL​)Πi​+PiL​ζ(piwin​(0)Πi​+PiA​λi​)=Πi​−PiL​[(1−ζpiwin​(0))Πi​−ζPiA​λi​]​

The bracket is the expected loss from being sued: the profit lost when the project does not survive without an appeal, net of the option value of appealing. Litigation risk deters entry whenever Wilit<ΠiW_i^{lit}<\Pi_iWilit​<Πi​, and a lower appeal cost CAC_ACA​ raises λi\lambda_iλi​ and hence ViV_iVi​, which is the channel of the fee-shifting counterfactual.

Start from the entry rule: a potential developer enters when the expected payoff of equation (6), net of the fixed entry cost, exceeds a private entry shock,

ei=1  ⟺  εientr≤Vi(Sc,xi)−CEe_i=1\iff \varepsilon_i^{entr}\le V_i(S_c,x_i)-C_Eei​=1⟺εientr​≤Vi​(Sc​,xi​)−CE​

The payoff of staying out is normalized to zero. Assume εientr\varepsilon_i^{entr}εientr​ is standard logistic, with CDF

Λ(x)=ex1+ex\Lambda(x)=\frac{e^{x}}{1+e^{x}}Λ(x)=1+exex​

This is the distribution of the difference of two independent type-I extreme value shocks, one attached to each option. The entry probability is the CDF evaluated at the threshold:

Pr⁡(ei=1)=Pr⁡(εientr≤Vi−CE)=Λ(Vi−CE)=exp⁡(Vi(Sc,xi)−CE)1+exp⁡(Vi(Sc,xi)−CE)\begin{aligned} \Pr(e_i=1)&=\Pr\left(\varepsilon_i^{entr}\le V_i-C_E\right)\\ &=\Lambda\left(V_i-C_E\right)\\ &=\frac{\exp\left(V_i(S_c,x_i)-C_E\right)}{1+\exp\left(V_i(S_c,x_i)-C_E\right)} \end{aligned}Pr(ei​=1)​=Pr(εientr​≤Vi​−CE​)=Λ(Vi​−CE​)=1+exp(Vi​(Sc​,xi​)−CE​)exp(Vi​(Sc​,xi​)−CE​)​​

Two properties are used later. The response to any payoff shifter is largest for marginal projects,

∂Pr⁡(ei=1)∂Vi=Pr⁡(ei=1)(1−Pr⁡(ei=1))\frac{\partial\Pr(e_i=1)}{\partial V_i}=\Pr(e_i=1)\left(1-\Pr(e_i=1)\right)∂Vi​∂Pr(ei​=1)​=Pr(ei​=1)(1−Pr(ei​=1))

and the log-odds of entry equal Vi−CEV_i-C_EVi​−CE​, so CEC_ECE​ is pinned down by the overall level of entry. Because rivals' actions do not enter ViV_iVi​, the simultaneous entry game reduces to independent binary choices, and expected entry in market ccc is the sum of these probabilities over the IcI_cIc​ potential projects.

The scale of the shock is fixed at one, so every payoff parameter is measured relative to the dispersion of εientr\varepsilon_i^{entr}εientr​ (see the remark under equation (4)). In the simulation the shock is not drawn independently: it is generated from the correlated normal draw of equation (16), which leaves this marginal probability unchanged.

This is an assumed reduced form for the probability that a litigated project ultimately survives, as a function of the developer's appellate engagement aia_iai​. It deliberately nests every procedural path: when ai=0a_i=0ai​=0 it is the probability of surviving when the developer neither appeals a loss nor defends a win against the opponent's appeal; when ai=1a_i=1ai​=1 it is the probability of ultimate success with appellate engagement. The index contains a constant γ0\gamma_0γ0​, the legal environment LcL_cLc​ (past cases, negative outcomes, precedents), the shifters ziz_izi​ and the engagement effect γa\gamma_aγa​, expected to be positive.

What matters for behavior is the gain in the survival probability from engaging,

piwin(1)−piwin(0)=Λ(γ0+γL′Lc+γz′zi+γa)−Λ(γ0+γL′Lc+γz′zi)p_i^{win}(1)-p_i^{win}(0)=\Lambda\left(\gamma_0+\gamma_L^{\prime}L_c+\gamma_z^{\prime}z_i+\gamma_a\right)-\Lambda\left(\gamma_0+\gamma_L^{\prime}L_c+\gamma_z^{\prime}z_i\right)piwin​(1)−piwin​(0)=Λ(γ0​+γL′​Lc​+γz′​zi​+γa​)−Λ(γ0​+γL′​Lc​+γz′​zi​)

which has the sign of γa\gamma_aγa​ and, for small γa\gamma_aγa​, is approximately

γa piwin(0)(1−piwin(0))\gamma_a\,p_i^{win}(0)\left(1-p_i^{win}(0)\right)γa​piwin​(0)(1−piwin​(0))

so engagement matters most for cases that are close calls. This gain multiplies Πi\Pi_iΠi​ in the incremental value of appealing in equation (11), and piwin(0)p_i^{win}(0)piwin​(0) is the baseline term of the continuation value in equation (12). Precedent enters through γL\gamma_LγL​: a clearer legal environment changes the chance of prevailing.

The parameters are identified from appeal win rates, overall and across bins of the legal environment. Two caveats. The estimated vector γ\gammaγ has only 4 elements, which the estimates table reports as γ0\gamma_0γ0​ and three loadings γL\gamma_LγL​; no separate estimates of γz\gamma_zγz​ or γa\gamma_aγa​ are reported, so the gain above is not pinned down by reported parameters. And with the estimate γ0=−4.977\gamma_0=-4.977γ0​=−4.977, the baseline survival probability at Lc=0L_c=0Lc​=0 is Λ(−4.977)\Lambda(-4.977)Λ(−4.977), about 0.007, so survival relies heavily on the legal-environment terms.

This is the expected private payoff of a litigated developer who chooses appellate engagement ai∈{0,1}a_i\in\{0,1\}ai​∈{0,1}, before the appeal shock. It is a lottery over two outcomes: with probability piwin(ai)p_i^{win}(a_i)piwin​(ai​) from equation (8) the project survives and yields Πi\Pi_iΠi​ from equation (5); otherwise it is cancelled and yields zero. The appeal cost CAC_ACA​ is paid upfront if and only if ai=1a_i=1ai​=1, whatever the outcome:

Uilit(ai)=piwin(ai) Πi+(1−piwin(ai))⋅0−aiCAU_i^{lit}(a_i)=p_i^{win}(a_i)\,\Pi_i+\left(1-p_i^{win}(a_i)\right)\cdot 0-a_iC_AUilit​(ai​)=piwin​(ai​)Πi​+(1−piwin​(ai​))⋅0−ai​CA​

The two values are

Uilit(0)=piwin(0) Πi,Uilit(1)=piwin(1) Πi−CAU_i^{lit}(0)=p_i^{win}(0)\,\Pi_i,\qquad U_i^{lit}(1)=p_i^{win}(1)\,\Pi_i-C_AUilit​(0)=piwin​(0)Πi​,Uilit​(1)=piwin​(1)Πi​−CA​

The form embeds several assumptions. The developer is risk neutral. The payoff after losing is zero, so the permitting cost inside Πi\Pi_iΠi​ is avoided when the project is cancelled, and there are no damages or lower-court legal fees. CAC_ACA​ is a constant, common to all projects and in the same units as Πi\Pi_iΠi​ (millions of dollars; the estimate is 0.536); it is identified from the overall appeal frequency among litigated projects and its variation across caseload and legal-environment bins. Finally, only private stakes appear: the value of the precedent that an appeal may create, equation (14), is absent, which is the source of the externality.

The difference Uilit(1)−Uilit(0)U_i^{lit}(1)-U_i^{lit}(0)Uilit​(1)−Uilit​(0) drives the appeal probability in equation (10) and is named λi\lambda_iλi​ in equation (11); the level Uilit(0)U_i^{lit}(0)Uilit​(0) is the baseline term of the continuation value in equation (12).

Start from the appeal rule: a litigated developer engages in appellate proceedings when the payoff of equation (9) from doing so, net of a private appeal shock, exceeds the payoff from not doing so,

ai=1  ⟺  Uilit(1)−εiappeal≥Uilit(0)  ⟺  εiappeal≤Uilit(1)−Uilit(0)a_i=1\iff U_i^{lit}(1)-\varepsilon_i^{appeal}\ge U_i^{lit}(0)\iff \varepsilon_i^{appeal}\le U_i^{lit}(1)-U_i^{lit}(0)ai​=1⟺Uilit​(1)−εiappeal​≥Uilit​(0)⟺εiappeal​≤Uilit​(1)−Uilit​(0)

The shock can be read as an idiosyncratic component of the appeal cost. Assume it is standard logistic with CDF Λ(x)=ex/(1+ex)\Lambda(x)=e^{x}/(1+e^{x})Λ(x)=ex/(1+ex). Then

Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)=Λ(Uilit(1)−Uilit(0))=exp⁡(Uilit(1)−Uilit(0))1+exp⁡(Uilit(1)−Uilit(0))\begin{aligned} \Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)&=\Lambda\left(U_i^{lit}(1)-U_i^{lit}(0)\right)\\ &=\frac{\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)-U_i^{lit}(0)\right)}{1+\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)-U_i^{lit}(0)\right)} \end{aligned}Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)​=Λ(Uilit​(1)−Uilit​(0))=1+exp(Uilit​(1)−Uilit​(0))exp(Uilit​(1)−Uilit​(0))​​

Multiply numerator and denominator by exp⁡(Uilit(0))\exp(U_i^{lit}(0))exp(Uilit​(0)) to obtain the symmetric binary-logit form of the target:

Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)=exp⁡(Uilit(1))exp⁡(Uilit(0))+exp⁡(Uilit(1))\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)=\frac{\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)\right)}{\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(0)\right)+\exp\left(U_i^{lit}(1)\right)}Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)=exp(Uilit​(0))+exp(Uilit​(1))exp(Uilit​(1))​

By equation (11) the payoff difference is λi\lambda_iλi​, so the result can be written compactly as

Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)=Λ(λi)=Λ((piwin(1)−piwin(0))Πi−CA)\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)=\Lambda(\lambda_i)=\Lambda\left(\left(p_i^{win}(1)-p_i^{win}(0)\right)\Pi_i-C_A\right)Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)=Λ(λi​)=Λ((piwin​(1)−piwin​(0))Πi​−CA​)

The appeal probability rises with the stake Πi\Pi_iΠi​ (when engagement raises the survival probability) and falls with CAC_ACA​; a project with λi=0\lambda_i=0λi​=0 appeals half of the time. The paper prints the numerator as the exponential of Vilit(1)V_i^{lit}(1)Vilit​(1), which is a typo for Uilit(1)U_i^{lit}(1)Uilit​(1); the note has corrected it. In the simulation the appeal shock is generated from the correlated draw of equation (16), so among litigated projects it is not a random draw from the logistic distribution.

Although stated as a definition, λi\lambda_iλi​ is the difference between the two latent payoffs of equation (9). Evaluate equation (9) at the two actions:

The first term is the expected private benefit of engaging: the increase in the survival probability from equation (8) times the stake from equation (5). The second term is the cost. Ignoring the shock, appealing pays when

For example, with the estimated appeal cost of 0.536 million dollars and a gain in survival probability of 0.2, only projects with Πi\Pi_iΠi​ of at least 2.68 million dollars have a positive incremental value. λi\lambda_iλi​ is the single index of the appeal decision, since equation (10) equals Λ(λi)\Lambda(\lambda_i)Λ(λi​), and it is the option-value term in the continuation value of equation (12). It contains only private stakes; the social counterpart adds the precedent externality, equation (15). Note that λi\lambda_iλi​ is measured in million dollars and is unbounded, unlike the weight between zero and one that the paper denotes by the same symbol in the externality section.

The continuation value is the expected Stage 2 payoff, taken before the appeal shock is realized, and then scaled by ζ\zetaζ. Write PiA≡Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1)P_i^{A}\equiv\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)PiA​≡Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1) from equation (10). Average the latent payoffs of equation (9) over the appeal decision:

using Uilit(0)=piwin(0) ΠiU_i^{lit}(0)=p_i^{win}(0)\,\Pi_iUilit​(0)=piwin​(0)Πi​ and equation (11). The first term is what the developer gets by staying passive; the second is the probability of appealing times the incremental value of doing so. Multiplying by ζ\zetaζ gives the target:

Wilit=ζ(piwin(0) Πi+PiAλi)W_i^{lit}=\zeta\left(p_i^{win}(0)\,\Pi_i+P_i^{A}\lambda_i\right)Wilit​=ζ(piwin​(0)Πi​+PiA​λi​)

Not every appellate decision becomes binding precedent. This equation is the assumed probability that an appeal by project iii produces one. The index contains a constant ψ0\psi_0ψ0​, the legal environment LcL_cLc​ (past cases, negative-outcome cases, existing precedents) and institutional legal characteristics ziz_izi​ of the case: whether it is heard in an appellate or a high court, whether there were multiple motions, whether the decision was affirmed, remanded or a summary judgment, and whether relief was granted against the permitting authority. The developer's action aia_iai​ and its payoff Πi\Pi_iΠi​ are deliberately excluded: conditional on an appeal, the courts decide what becomes precedent, independently of who wins. Per litigated project, the probability of a new precedent is therefore

Pr⁡(precedenti=1∣Li=1)=Pr⁡(ai=1∣Li=1) ψi\Pr(\text{precedent}_i=1\mid L_i=1)=\Pr(a_i=1\mid L_i=1)\,\psi_iPr(precedenti​=1∣Li​=1)=Pr(ai​=1∣Li​=1)ψi​

so developers affect precedent formation only through the appeal probability of equation (10).

This exclusion is what allows the slopes ψL\psi_LψL​ and ψz\psi_zψz​ (10 parameters) to be estimated outside the model on observed appeals, using variation in court level and case characteristics, while only the constant ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ is estimated by SMM, equation (19), to match the overall number of precedents (157 in data and model; the estimate 0.062 has a very large standard error). The reported outside estimates are marginal effects, for example 0.57 for a high court and 0.34 for an appellate court.

An inconsistency to keep in mind: the equation is written with the logistic CDF Λ\LambdaΛ, but the outside estimation is described as a probit, which would use the standard normal CDF Φ\PhiΦ. The two links are close after rescaling the index by roughly 1.6, but the coefficients are not interchangeable. ψi\psi_iψi​ does not enter any private payoff; it matters for the simulated count of precedents and it is the natural weight in the external benefit Ωi\Omega_iΩi​ of equation (15).

The formula is a first-order valuation of one additional precedent for the next cohort of projects. The paper states it without derivation and does not define δα\delta_\alphaδα​ and δβ\delta_\betaδβ​ precisely; the following reading reproduces it.

Consider one future potential project. With probability 1−pˉlit1-\bar{p}^{lit}1−pˉ​lit it is not litigated and with probability pˉlit\bar{p}^{lit}pˉ​lit it is. Suppose one more precedent raises the probability that the project goes ahead by δα>0\delta_\alpha>0δα​>0 in the non-litigated state (clearer standards, smoother permitting) and by δβ>0\delta_\beta>0δβ​>0 in the litigated state (a better chance of surviving the lower court). Averaging over the two states, the change in the probability of going ahead is

Δq=δα(1−pˉlit)+δβ pˉlit\Delta q=\delta_\alpha\left(1-\bar{p}^{lit}\right)+\delta_\beta\,\bar{p}^{lit}Δq=δα​(1−pˉ​lit)+δβ​pˉ​lit

Δq⋅κcomp Πˉfut\Delta q\cdot\kappa^{comp}\,\bar{\Pi}^{fut}Δq⋅κcompΠˉfut

Precedent is non-rival, so the same gain accrues to each of the NfutN^{fut}Nfut potential entrants of the next cohort. Summing gives the target:

Ω=[δα(1−pˉlit)+δβ pˉlit]κcomp ΠˉfutNfut\Omega=\left[\delta_\alpha\left(1-\bar{p}^{lit}\right)+\delta_\beta\,\bar{p}^{lit}\right]\kappa^{comp}\,\bar{\Pi}^{fut}N^{fut}Ω=[δα​(1−pˉ​lit)+δβ​pˉ​lit]κcompΠˉfutNfut

It counts one future cohort only, without discounting or the durable value of precedent for later cohorts, so it is a lower bound in that dimension. It abstracts from the induced change in entry. And Πˉfut\bar{\Pi}^{fut}Πˉfut is defined conditional on completion, which is why κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp appears explicitly here, whereas Πi\Pi_iΠi​ in equation (5) already contains it. The paper does not estimate δα\delta_\alphaδα​, δβ\delta_\betaδβ​ or compute Ω\OmegaΩ; the externality is instead quantified through counterfactual entry. Finally, this Ω\OmegaΩ is unrelated to the covariance matrix of moments denoted by the same letter in equations (20) and (21).

The under-investment result follows from the decision rule. The developer appeals when λi≥εiappeal\lambda_i\ge\varepsilon_i^{appeal}λi​≥εiappeal​, while a planner who internalizes the externality would have the developer appeal when λi+Ωi≥εiappeal\lambda_i+\Omega_i\ge\varepsilon_i^{appeal}λi​+Ωi​≥εiappeal​. Since Λ\LambdaΛ is increasing and Ωi>0\Omega_i>0Ωi​>0,

and for a small externality the gap is approximately

Piappeal(1−Piappeal)ΩiP_i^{appeal}\left(1-P_i^{appeal}\right)\Omega_iPiappeal​(1−Piappeal​)Ωi​

Private appeals, and hence precedents, are too few. A per-appeal subsidy equal to Ωi\Omega_iΩi​, equivalent to lowering CAC_ACA​ by that amount, restores the planner's rule, which motivates the fee-shifting and legal-insurance counterfactuals that reduce CAC_ACA​.

This assumption is how the model handles selection on unobservables. Observed lawsuits and appeals are not a random sample of projects: financial resources, legal sophistication, project quality and risk tolerance affect entry, exposure to litigation and the willingness to appeal at once. The three latent shocks are therefore drawn jointly from a trivariate normal with unit variances, so Σ\SigmaΣ is a correlation matrix. ρEL\rho_{EL}ρEL​ links entry and litigation shocks, ρLA\rho_{LA}ρLA​ links litigation and appeal shocks, and ρEA\rho_{EA}ρEA​ links entry and appeal shocks and is normalized to zero.

The normal draws are mapped to uniforms uij=Φ(νij)u_i^{j}=\Phi(\nu_i^{j})uij​=Φ(νij​) and used in the logit choices. The event that a uniform is below a logit probability is the event that a logistic shock is below the index, so the implied structural shocks are

εij=Λ−1(Φ(νij)),j∈{entry,lit,appeal}\varepsilon_i^{j}=\Lambda^{-1}\left(\Phi\left(\nu_i^{j}\right)\right),\qquad j\in\{entry,lit,appeal\}εij​=Λ−1(Φ(νij​)),j∈{entry,lit,appeal}

This is a Gaussian copula with logistic marginals: each stage keeps the marginal logit formulas of equations (7) and (10), while the dependence across stages comes from Σ\SigmaΣ. Setting all correlations to zero returns independent logits.

Σ\SigmaΣ must be positive definite. With ρEA=0\rho_{EA}=0ρEA​=0 its determinant is

det⁡Σ=1−ρEL2−ρLA2\det\Sigma=1-\rho_{EL}^{2}-\rho_{LA}^{2}detΣ=1−ρEL2​−ρLA2​

so the two correlations must satisfy ρEL2+ρLA2<1\rho_{EL}^{2}+\rho_{LA}^{2}<1ρEL2​+ρLA2​<1. The raw estimates 0.922 and 0.764 violate this, which is why they are reported together with implied correlations of 0.726 and 0.441. Those numbers are reproduced by a transformation that enforces the constraint,

ρEL=tanh⁡(0.922)≈0.727,ρLA=tanh⁡(0.764)1−ρEL2≈0.442\rho_{EL}=\tanh(0.922)\approx 0.727,\qquad \rho_{LA}=\tanh(0.764)\sqrt{1-\rho_{EL}^{2}}\approx 0.442ρEL​=tanh(0.922)≈0.727,ρLA​=tanh(0.764)1−ρEL2​​≈0.442

although the paper does not state the mapping; this is an inference from the reported figures.

The normalization ρEA=0\rho_{EA}=0ρEA​=0 imposes marginal independence of the entry and appeal shocks. It does not make them independent conditional on the litigation shock: the implied partial correlation is

ρEA⋅L=−ρEL ρLA(1−ρEL2)(1−ρLA2)\rho_{EA\cdot L}=\frac{-\rho_{EL}\,\rho_{LA}}{\sqrt{\left(1-\rho_{EL}^{2}\right)\left(1-\rho_{LA}^{2}\right)}}ρEA⋅L​=(1−ρEL2​)(1−ρLA2​)​−ρEL​ρLA​​

which is negative when both correlations are positive, so the paper's verbal justification (no direct correlation conditional on litigation exposure) does not match the restriction exactly. Identification uses the excluded shifters: entry across bins of the lower-court caseload z2z_2z2​ for ρEL\rho_{EL}ρEL​, and appeal rates of litigated projects across z2z_2z2​ bins for ρLA\rho_{LA}ρLA​.

These two accounting identities build the revenue side of the computed NPV for a potential entrant. MWiMW_iMWi​ is nameplate capacity in megawatts, bootstrapped from actual entrants in the same county-year (or state-year). CFiCF_iCFi​ is the state-level, technology-specific capacity factor, the fraction of nameplate output actually produced on average. CurtailiCurtail_iCurtaili​ is the share of potential generation that is curtailed. The number 8760 is the hours in a year, so QiQ_iQi​ is annual generation in megawatt-hours. PiwholesaleP_i^{wholesale}Piwholesale​ is the average peak-hour wholesale price and PippaP_i^{ppa}Pippa​ the regional PPA price, both in dollars per megawatt-hour, so RiR_iRi​ is annual revenue in dollars.

An illustration: a 100 MW project with a capacity factor of 0.35 and curtailment of 3 percent produces

Qi=100×0.35×0.97×8760≈297,400 MWhQ_i=100\times 0.35\times 0.97\times 8760\approx 297{,}400\ \text{MWh}Qi​=100×0.35×0.97×8760≈297,400 MWh

and at an effective price of 50 dollars per megawatt-hour it earns

Ri≈297,400×50≈14.9 million dollars per yearR_i\approx 297{,}400\times 50\approx 14.9\ \text{million dollars per year}Ri​≈297,400×50≈14.9 million dollars per year

The construction is deliberately coarse. Generation is linear in capacity, so revenue per megawatt varies only by technology, state, region and year, not with site quality. The effective price is the sum of a wholesale price and a PPA price; a real project typically sells under one arrangement or a mix, so the sum is a modelling choice that tends to overstate the price level. Peak-hour prices are used even though wind and solar output profiles differ. Production tax credits and other subsidies are not included.

These measurement errors are one reason why the model does not take the computed profit at face value but rescales it with θπ\theta_\piθπ​ in equation (4). RiR_iRi​ feeds the NPV formula in equation (18), and the resulting profit is the source of the entry variation across NPV bins that identifies θπ\theta_\piθπ​.

The NPV is the present value of a constant annual operating margin received for 25 years. Since 1−v=r/(1+r)1-v=r/(1+r)1−v=r/(1+r), we have v/(1−v)=1/rv/(1-v)=1/rv/(1−v)=1/r, and therefore

NPVi=(Ri−CiO&M)×1−(1+r)−25rNPV_i=\left(R_i-C_i^{O\&M}\right)\times\frac{1-(1+r)^{-25}}{r}NPVi​=(Ri​−CiO&M​)×r1−(1+r)−25​

This vector lists the 23 parameters estimated jointly by the simulated method of moments, grouped by the block of the model they govern. The entry and permitting block has 14: the entry cost CEC_ECE​ of equation (7), the 12 elements of α\alphaα in the permitting cost of equation (2) (a constant, 3 legal, 2 permitting and 6 county loadings) and the profit scaling θπ\theta_\piθπ​ of equation (4). The appeal and precedent block has 7: the appeal cost CAC_ACA​ of equation (9), the sensitivity ζ\zetaζ of equation (12), the 4 elements of γ\gammaγ in the win probability of equation (8), and the constant ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ of the precedent probability in equation (13). The selection block has the 2 free correlations of equation (16). The count is

1+12+1⏟Entry / Permit+1+1+4+1⏟Appeal / Precedent+2⏟Selection Corr=23\underbrace{1+12+1}_{\text{Entry / Permit}}+\underbrace{1+1+4+1}_{\text{Appeal / Precedent}}+\underbrace{2}_{\text{Selection Corr}}=23Entry / Permit1+12+1​​+Appeal / Precedent1+1+4+1​​+Selection Corr2​​=23

What is not in the vector is as informative. The calibrated objects (the litigation count ctlitct^{lit}ctlit and the completion probability κcomp\kappa^{comp}κcomp) and the 10 slopes of ψ\psiψ, estimated by a probit outside the model, are held fixed. The coefficients β\betaβ of the litigation probability in equation (3) are not estimated at all, because litigation is assigned by the exponential race. The correlation ρEA\rho_{EA}ρEA​ is normalized to zero. And since the estimated γ\gammaγ consists of the constant and three legal-environment loadings, γz\gamma_zγz​ and γa\gamma_aγa​ of equation (8) have no reported estimates.

Each parameter is tied to specific moments: CEC_ECE​ to overall entry; α\alphaα to entry by bins of the legal, permitting and county variables; θπ\theta_\piθπ​ to entry by NPV bins; CAC_ACA​ to appeals among litigated projects; γ\gammaγ to appeal win rates; ψ0\psi_0ψ0​ to the overall precedent count; the correlations to entry and appeal across bins of the lower-court caseload z2z_2z2​. With 40 moments and 23 parameters the model is overidentified by 17 restrictions, which is what the estimator of equation (20) exploits.

This defines the SMM estimator. For a candidate Θ\ThetaΘ (the vector of equation (19)) the model is simulated: a pool of potential entrants per county-year, continuation values by backward induction, entry by the logit of equation (7), litigation assigned by the exponential race, appeals by equation (10), then outcomes and precedents. This produces simulated moments M(Θ)M(\Theta)M(Θ), mostly counts within bins, which are compared with their empirical counterparts MMM. The kkk-th element of ggg is the percentage deviation

gk(Θ)=Mk(Θ)−MkMk,k=1,…,40g_k(\Theta)=\frac{M_k(\Theta)-M_k}{M_k},\qquad k=1,\dots,40gk​(Θ)=Mk​Mk​(Θ)−Mk​​,k=1,…,40

Percentage deviations make moments of very different magnitude comparable (overall entry is about 15,570, while some appeal bins contain fewer than 10 cases). The objective is the quadratic form

g(Θ)′Wg(Θ)=∑k=140∑l=140gk(Θ) Wkl gl(Θ)g(\Theta)^{\prime}Wg(\Theta)=\sum_{k=1}^{40}\sum_{l=1}^{40}g_k(\Theta)\,W_{kl}\,g_l(\Theta)g(Θ)′Wg(Θ)=k=1∑40​l=1∑40​gk​(Θ)Wkl​gl​(Θ)

which is zero only if every simulated moment equals its target. WWW decides which moments matter most. The choice W=Ω^−1W=\hat{\Omega}^{-1}W=Ω^−1, the inverse of the bootstrap covariance matrix of the empirical moments (200 replications), down-weights noisy moments and accounts for their correlation; it is the efficient choice and it simplifies the variance formula in equation (21). If Ω^\hat{\Omega}Ω^ were diagonal the objective would reduce to

∑k=140gk(Θ)2Ω^kk\sum_{k=1}^{40}\frac{g_k(\Theta)^{2}}{\hat{\Omega}_{kk}}k=1∑40​Ω^kk​gk​(Θ)2​

One point of consistency is left implicit. ggg is in percentage terms, so for WWW to be the efficient weight Ω^\hat{\Omega}Ω^ must be the covariance of the moments in the same relative units rather than of the raw counts; with D=diag⁡(M1,…,M40)D=\operatorname{diag}(M_1,\dots,M_{40})D=diag(M1​,…,M40​) and ΩM\Omega_MΩM​ the covariance of the raw moments, the appropriate matrix is

Because the moments are counts of simulated discrete outcomes, the objective is a step function of Θ\ThetaΘ and is not differentiable, which is why a genetic algorithm rather than a gradient method is used. With 40 moments and 23 parameters the minimized objective is not zero. Here Ω^\hat{\Omega}Ω^ is the covariance of moments, not the social surplus of equation (14).

The limit distribution follows from the standard argument for minimum-distance estimators. Let g(Θ)g(\Theta)g(Θ) be the moment vector of equation (20), G=∂g(Θ)/∂Θ′G=\partial g(\Theta)/\partial\Theta^{\prime}G=∂g(Θ)/∂Θ′ its Jacobian (40 rows, 23 columns, full column rank), and SSS the number of observations.
